subject: CAIQ: inference telemetry & KV-cache evidence request
messages:
From: Anoop Reddy <a.reddy@mediastream.com>
To: diego_fernandez@redwood.example.com
Cc: Gina Morales <gina@securityevals.io>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 08:22:00 -0800
Subject: CAIQ evidence - runtime telemetry & KV cache handling

Diego --

Thanks for taking this. We're in the final leg of our cloud security assessment and CSA's CAIQ reviewers flagged a few controls where they want concrete runtime telemetry evidence for inference services. High-level ask: a mapping showing which CAIQ questions map to artifacts for inference telemetry, plus example artifacts we can present to the auditor. Specifically they called out:

- evidence that (a) inference request/response telemetry is logged and retained, (b) prefix/KV cache eviction and access is observable, and (c) token-level latency and routing traces are attributable to a service owner.

Can you share a short crosswalk and sample artifacts (logs or exports) we can hand to the auditor? We need scrubbed samples (no PII or customer prompts) and a short README with export steps. Target deadline: next Fri (2026-02-19).

Attaching the CAIQ sections they highlighted in-line below. Happy to jump on a 30m call if helpful.

Thanks,
Anoop Reddy
Security & Compliance Manager
Mediastream

---
Attached to their original: CAIQ extract (inline), but they asked for evidence only in follow-up.

From: diego_fernandez@redwood.example.com
To: Anoop Reddy <a.reddy@mediastream.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.example.com, jonas_weber@redwood.example.com
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: CAIQ evidence - runtime telemetry & KV cache handling

Anoop —

Appreciate the clear ask. We'll produce a CAIQ crosswalk focused on inference runtime telemetry and provide scrubbed samples plus a short export README. Plan below: 

1) Deliverable: caiq_inference_telemetry_crosswalk.xlsx (mapping: CAIQ question -> control area -> artifact sample).
2) Artifacts: 
   - kv_cache_log_sample_scrubbed.tar.gz (eviction/access events, scrubbed IDs)
   - token_latency_trace_sample.jsonl (per-request latency trace, anonymized) — we'll include a short summary instead of full JSONL in the first pass.
3) Instructions: telemetry_export_instructions.md with commands and how we scrub PII.
4) Owners & contacts: Kim (telemetry export + scrub), Jonas (control mapping / instrumentation owners), Priyom (security review & signing).
5) Timeline: initial crosswalk + README by Fri 2026-02-13 EOD PST; scrubbed artifacts by Tue 2026-02-17.

Kim/Jonas — can you confirm owner availability and whether the token trace can be summarized as a CSV instead of a full JSONL? We prefer small artifacts for initial reviewer consumption.

Anoop — if that timeline works we will send the Drive link and attach the primary crosswalk. If you need a tighter window, let me know and we can prioritize the README + one sample first.

Diego Fernandez
Sr. Security Solutions Manager
Redwood Inference

From: kimberly_park@redwood.example.com
To: diego_fernandez@redwood.example.com, kimberly_park@redwood.example.com
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.example.com, priyom_das@redwood.example.com
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: CAIQ evidence - runtime telemetry & KV cache handling

Diego / team — quick status and extraction notes.

- Owners: I'm available to run the exports and perform redaction; Jonas will validate control annotations. Priyom will review for sensitive data.
- What I'll produce: 
  * kv_cache_log_sample_scrubbed.tar.gz — compressed CSVs extracted from the KV cache access logs. Fields: timestamp, action (lookup/hit/miss/evict), bucket_name (redacted), event_id (scrubbed hash), sequence_len_estimate (no content). No prompt text, no embedding vectors, no raw inputs.
  * caiq_inference_telemetry_crosswalk.xlsx — mapping with suggested evidence artifacts and control owner columns.
  * telemetry_export_instructions.md — commands to pull logs from the telemetry pipeline, scrub steps, and a checklist.

- Export commands (high level):
  1) SSH to telemetrydump@prod-telemetry
  2) run: ./export_kv_access.sh --start 2026-01-01 --end 2026-01-31 --anonymize --out kv_sample.csv\  (script performs sha256 of ids and drops payload)
  3) tar & gzip, then checksum

- Token latency traces: Jonas recommends a summarized CSV (request_id_hash, p50_ms, p95_ms, routing_variant) rather than the full JSONL. That should satisfy the auditor for timing and routing evidence without exposing content.

I'll start the export today and aim to upload artifacts to the shared Drive folder (link will be posted to SEC-4827). Estimated upload: 2026-02-16.

Kim Park
Engineering Manager, Telemetry
Redwood Inference

From: diego_fernandez@redwood.example.com
To: Anoop Reddy <a.reddy@mediastream.com>
Cc: Gina Morales <gina@securityevals.io>, kimberly_park@redwood.example.com, jonas_weber@redwood.example.com, priyom_das@redwood.example.com
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 15:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: CAIQ evidence - runtime telemetry & KV cache handling

Anoop / Gina —

Attached is the initial package and a short summary of the mapping we think addresses the auditor's flagged CAIQ questions: 

Summary (high-level):
- CAIQ question: "Are runtime request/response logs captured and retained?"
  -> Artifact: caiq_inference_telemetry_crosswalk.xlsx (tab: RUNTIME_LOGGING), kv_cache_log_sample_scrubbed.tar.gz (sample of cache access events), telemetry_export_instructions.md

- CAIQ question: "Is access to caching and ephemeral stores logged and attributable?"
  -> Artifact: kv_cache_log_sample_scrubbed.tar.gz (eviction/access events with hashed ids), crosswalk mapping to control IDs and owner (Jonas)

- CAIQ question: "Is token latency and routing traceable to service owners?"
  -> Artifact: token_latency_summary.csv (summarized p50/p95 + routing variant), crosswalk row with owner (Priyom) and retention policy excerpt

What we uploaded to Drive: caiq_inference_telemetry_crosswalk.xlsx, kv_cache_log_sample_scrubbed.tar.gz, telemetry_export_instructions.md. Files are in this folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcdExampleDriveLink (SEC-4827).

Next steps: please review the crosswalk and confirm which CAIQ rows the reviewer will present first; if they want a live demo of the export we can schedule a 30-minute session next week.

Thanks — Diego
Sr. Security Solutions Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: caiq_inference_telemetry_crosswalk.xlsx (Excel workbook), kv_cache_log_sample_scrubbed.tar.gz (tar/gzip, CSVs inside), telemetry_export_instructions.md (text)
